subject: Egress approval & roles — private connector deployment
messages:
From: Matt Jordan <matt.jordan@corvushealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, sally.park@corvushealth.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: egress allowlist + ownership for private connector

Hi Rishi,

We're kicking off our private deployment for Corvus Health and need to close the network/egress requirements so our security team can sign off. Attached is our initial matrix (corvus-egress-requirements.xlsx) — it lists which hosts/services we expect the private connector to call and which ports/TLS modes our firewall will allow.

Two immediate asks:
- Who at Redwood is responsible for the control-plane outbound IPs (for audit + allowlisting)?
- Do you provide a single static NAT IP block we can put in our perimeter, or do you expect us to NAT/proxy from our side?

We'd like to map responsibilities and agree on an implementation timeline next week. Can you confirm owners and whether you need any forms from our ops team? CC'd Laura and Sally.

Thanks,
Matt
Matt Jordan
Head of Infrastructure, Corvus Health

Attachment: corvus-egress-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Matt Jordan <matt.jordan@corvushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: egress allowlist + ownership for private connector

Matt — thanks for the matrix, that's helpful. High level answers first:

- Redwood responsibilities: we own outbound connections from the connector agents to the Redwood control plane (health checks, metrics, model manifest fetches). We will provide a small set of static egress IPs for control-plane traffic and a documented port list.
- Customer responsibilities: the customer (Corvus) owns the network perimeter allowlist for incoming call-backs and any upstream vendor endpoints you choose to route through. If you prefer to NAT to a single IP on your side, that's acceptable; we only require the control-plane egress IPs to be allowed.

Proposed owners and next steps:
1) Corvus network team — confirm final allowlist and control window for changes (owner: Matt/Sally)
2) Redwood networking — publish final IP list and port sec to your inventory (owner: Laura)
3) Redwood infra (marissa) — provide runbook and automation scripts to validate connectivity and perform a test window

I'm attaching a short guideline PDF that lists the ports and recommended TLS modes and also describes our suggested proxy pattern if you want to centralize NAT on your side.

Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment early next week (Mon/Tue)? If you give us a preferred change window we can draft the acceptance checklist.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-egress-guidelines.pdf (PDF, 89KB)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Matt Jordan <matt.jordan@corvushealth.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: egress allowlist + ownership for private connector

Quick notes from a product/ops perspective:
- We will publish a short-lived set of static control-plane IPs (two /29s) for the managed control-plane endpoints; recommend you pin them in your firewall rather than using DNS-based allowlists.
- mTLS is strongly recommended for connector -> control-plane; if your environment can't do mTLS we can accept TLS with a pinned cert fingerprint as a fallback.
- DNS split-horizon is fine — just confirm the resolver for the connector environment.

Happy to join the call next week.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: Matt Jordan <matt.jordan@corvushealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: sally.park@corvushealth.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: egress allowlist + ownership for private connector

Thanks Rishi/Laura. Couple clarifying items from our security ops:
- Our perimeter team prefers inbound allowlists to be limited to /29 blocks only (no wider). Can you confirm the final block sizes?
- Do you expect any control-plane callbacks to originate from additional IPs (e.g., pools in other regions) that we'd need to include?
- Our firewall vendor requires the exact SNI and TLS versions; can you confirm SNI hostnames used by the connector and whether TLS1.3 is enforced?

I'm attaching our vendor firewall rules doc so you can see the constraints. Also, if we NAT from our side, would Redwood still need any outbound whitelisting on your end?

-Matt

Attachment: vendor-firewall-rules.docx (DOCX, 28KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Matt Jordan <matt.jordan@corvushealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: egress allowlist + ownership for private connector

Matt — forwarding a short extract from our infra runbook that should directly answer the vendor questions. Please confirm the listed values and we'll add them to the shared checklist.

----- runbook excerpt -----
Required control-plane egress (Redwood -> control plane):
- IPs: 34.198.120.16/29, 34.198.120.24/29 (two /29 blocks; will publish 6 usable IPs per block)
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS), 5222 (metrics/bidi), 10250 (agent heartbeat — TLS)
- SNI: control.redwood-inference.com
- TLS: prefer TLS1.3; fallback TLS1.2 allowed for legacy stacks
- mTLS: supported; cert rotation handled by Redwood every 30 days (we'll provide fingerprints in the runbook)
- Regional variations: none for initial GA — same IP blocks globally for managed control-plane endpoints

Validation and change window:
1) Corvus opens a ticket with your firewall change window date
2) Redwood infra runs connectivity tests and a simulated token exchange
3) If tests pass, we move to production cutover during the agreed window

Contact for change coordination: marissa_cole@redwood.ai — please include the ticket id in the subject.

----- end excerpt -----

Forwarding the vendor doc you attached below for reference.

— Marissa
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Matt Jordan <matt.jordan@corvushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: egress allowlist + ownership for private connector

Thanks everyone — summary and action items below.

Acceptance criteria (what Corvus needs to verify):
- Your perimeter firewall includes the two /29 blocks (34.198.120.16/29, 34.198.120.24/29) for control-plane egress.
- SNI control.redwood-inference.com allowed and TLS1.3 preferred.
- If you opt to NAT to a single IP, provide the post-NAT address and a brief justification; Redwood only requires the control-plane source IPs to be routable/allowed into your environment for any callbacks.
- Confirm change window by creating a ticket at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_shared_egress and add the firewall vendor doc and your desired maintenance window.

Proposed timeline:
- Corvus confirms owner + change window by EOD Thu 08/05
- Redwood publishes final runbook and IP fingerprints by 08/06
- Test window 08/09 (connectivity + simulated token exchange)

Open items:
- Matt: confirm whether you will NAT on your side (and provide post-NAT IP if so)
- Corvus: confirm vendor firewall supports TLS1.3 SNI (or request fallback)

I'll drop the final acceptance checklist into the shared folder and link it to your HubSpot deal.

Thanks — Rishi
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress-final-checklist.csv (CSV, 6KB)
